name: Prithvi Dharmaraj
title: Software Engineer
summary: Software Engineer with 2+ years building payment infrastructure at Amazon Pay, specializing in tokenization, card network integrations, and agentic payment systems. Experienced in designing high availability transaction systems with a focus on security and developer experience.

experience.title: Software Engineer 2
accomplishments: As a Software Engineer 2 on Amazon Pay, I lead the agentic tokenization orchestration efforts that power payment method acceptance for Amazon's AI-driven products in off-Amazon experiences, including Buy For Me and Alexa+. I also designed and own key features of the external transaction management system, which gives internal risk and fraud detection layers deeper visibility into how agentic transactions behave outside of Amazon's ecosystem. My work sits at the intersection of payment security and emerging agentic AI, ensuring that as these products scale, the underlying payment infrastructure remains secure, observable, and reliable.

experience.title: Software Engineer 1
accomplishments: I led a team of 8 engineers to design and implement a network token life-cycle management system that fundamentally simplified how payment service providers integrate with Amazon Pay. This involved owning the technical communication with major card networks (Visa, Mastercard, and Discover) to align on integration patterns for their tokenization platforms like VTS and MDES. Beyond tokenization, I drove merchant adoption by migrating PSD2 multi-factor authentication handling from legacy architecture to support new product launches, and designed a discrepancy handling system that automatically detects and surfaces invoicing issues from providers like Stripe to internal settlement stakeholders.

experience.title: Research Engineer
accomplishments: At GTRI's Sensors and Electromagnetic Applications Lab, I worked on an in-development digital radar system where I built custom internal C++ libraries for networking protocols including Telnet and Data Distribution Service (DDS), enabling reliable real-time communication between radar subsystems. I also redesigned the radar metric ingestion pipeline by developing a high-throughput HDF5 library in C++ that significantly improved how the system captured and stored large volumes of sensor data for downstream analysis.
